entries.psalms 142:6: He begs God to listen because he is brought very low, and admits his enemies are stronger than he is. It is honest and right to tell God you are weak and need him to rescue you.
entries.psalms 142:7: He asks God to free him from his prison so he can praise God's name, and he expects that good people will be encouraged by what God does for him. God's rescue of you is meant to become a reason for others to hope and praise too.
entries.psalms 140:1: David asks God to rescue him from people who want to hurt him. It reminds the reader that when others mean us harm, we can ask God to protect us.
entries.psalms 140:2: These people spend their time planning evil and stirring up conflict. It warns the reader that some people's hearts are set on causing trouble, not peace.
entries.psalms 140:3: Their words are as dangerous as snake venom, hurting people deeply. It reminds the reader that cruel words can do real damage, so we should be careful with our speech.
entries.psalms 140:4: David repeats his prayer for protection because his enemies are actively plotting to bring him down. It shows the reader that it is fine to keep asking God for help when danger continues.
entries.psalms 140:5: Proud men have set hidden traps to catch him without warning. It reminds the reader that some harm comes through secret schemes, and we need God's help to see and avoid them.
entries.psalms 140:6: David declares that the Lord is his God and asks him to listen to his prayer. It encourages the reader to speak to God personally and trust that he hears.
entries.psalms 140:7: David remembers that God has been his strength and shield in past battles. It reminds the reader to recall how God has protected them before and take courage from it.
entries.psalms 140:8: David asks God not to let the wicked succeed or become proud. It reminds the reader that it is right to pray that evil plans will fail rather than prosper.
entries.psalms 140:9: David asks that the harm his enemies plan with their words would fall back on them. It expresses a longing for justice, that people who plot evil would not get away with it.
entries.psalms 140:10: David uses strong pictures of fire and deep water to ask God to stop these violent men for good. It shows how deeply he feels the threat and how much he wants evil to be ended.
entries.psalms 140:11: He prays that people who speak evil and use violence will not last long on the earth. It reflects the hope that cruelty will not go unpunished.
entries.psalms 140:12: David is confident that God will defend the poor and stand up for those who are mistreated. It gives the reader hope that God cares about injustice and will act on behalf of the helpless.
entries.psalms 140:13: Those who do right will thank God, and those who are faithful will live in his presence. It encourages the reader that trusting God ends in praise and belonging to him.
entries.psalms 141:1: David is urgently asking God to listen to his prayer, as if he can't wait for an answer. It reminds the reader that it's okay to call on God right away when you're in trouble.
entries.psalms 141:2: He pictures his prayer rising to God like the smoke of incense and his raised hands like the evening sacrifice at the temple. It means God values our prayers as an offering, so we can bring them honestly.
entries.psalms 141:3: He asks God to guard his mouth like a door that keeps watch. It's a prayer for self-control in what we say, since careless words can do real damage.
entries.psalms 141:4: He asks God to keep his heart from wanting evil and to keep him from joining in with people who do wrong, even the pleasant parts of their wrongdoing. It's a prayer to stay away from temptation rather than drift into it.
entries.psalms 141:5: He would rather be corrected by good people than be flattered or anointed by the wicked, and he commits himself to prayer when evil people do harm. It means we should welcome honest correction and respond to wrongdoing by praying, not by joining in.
entries.psalms 141:6: He expects that when the wicked leaders are judged, people will finally listen to his words because they are true and good. It's a hope that right words will be vindicated in the end.
entries.psalms 141:7: He describes his people as crushed and scattered, like ground broken up by a plough, near the edge of death. It expresses deep suffering and the feeling of being worn down.
entries.psalms 141:8: Even in that low place, he keeps his eyes on God and puts his hope in him, asking not to be left to die. It shows that trust in God can hold steady in the worst times.
entries.psalms 141:9: He asks God to keep him out of the traps and schemes that evil people have set for him. It's a prayer for protection from those who mean harm.
entries.psalms 141:10: He prays that the wicked will fall into their own traps while he escapes safely. It's a plea for justice, asking God to let evil backfire on those who plan it.
